scope: Theorem 1.1 (Periodic initialization) of the manuscript “Geometric Programs for Solenoidal Forcing” (preprints/Geometric-Programs-for-Solenoidal-Forcing-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1e54090582721ee2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a computable viscosity ν > 0. From a deterministic one-tape machine, with head moves in {−1, 0, 1}, and a finite input, one can effectively construct a smooth force on T3 1 such that: (i) The force is divergence free, has zero spatial mean, and is one-periodic from time zero. Equation (1) has a global smooth solution with pressure zero, unique in the stated classical class. (ii) The velocity is one-periodic, vanishes near every integer time, has zero instantaneous self- advection, and has uniformly bounded kinetic energy. Every mixed derivative of force and velocity is globally bounded. (iii) For the fixed label a∗ = (1/4, 1/2, 1/4) and fixed open strip O = {1/2 < x1 < 7/8}, the material trajectory enters O at a finite real time exactly when the machine halts, including an initially halted machine. The construction may use one Cartesian velocity component at a time. For arbitrary fixed real ν > 0 the same formulas hold and are effective relative to that viscosity.
